items.problem: A correct migration with zero deferred files always emits a spurious '[WARN] MIGRATION-DEFERRED.md exists with content but mapping has no defer rows — check consistency', pulling the dev-agent into investigating a non-issue at the finish line.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 3364 & 3418 (WARN on both validator runs); turns 35-36 the dev-agent opens MIGRATION-DEFERRED.md to check it, on a 100/100 app. Root cause found by grepping the two scripts: Initialize seeds '| (none) | — |' (Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 line 480) but Validate only treats the file as clean if it matches 'No items deferred' (Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 line 267).
items.root_cause: The bootstrap seeder and the validator use inconsistent empty-deferred sentinels, so the zero-defer case (the common case) always trips the else-branch WARN.
items.change: Align the empty-deferred sentinel across the two scripts: (1) Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 now writes an explicit '_No items deferred._' note in the zero-defer branch; (2) Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 now also accepts the '| (none) |' placeholder row as clean (defensive for already-seeded/hand-edited projects). Both encode one rule: an empty deferred list is a valid, expected state and must not produce a WARN.
items.expected_effect: Zero-defer migrations pass the DEFERRED.md consistency check cleanly; the dev-agent no longer spends turns investigating a benign WARN.
items.falsifiable_check: Re-run Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 on any migration with no deferred files → it prints '[PASS] No defer rows; MIGRATION-DEFERRED.md correctly notes ...' instead of the '[WARN] ... check consistency'. A genuine inconsistency (mapping has no defer rows but DEFERRED.md still lists a real file) still WARNs — verified: '| Foo.cs | speech |' stays flagged.

deferred_to_human: Tier-0/style: the scaffold pastes non-nullable-annotated UWP code into a net10 project with <Nullable>enable>, producing ~24-48 CS86xx nullable warnings on every migration. Harmless (0 WUI analyzer warnings, build/score unaffected) but noisy; consider whether the scaffold csproj should set <Nullable>disable</Nullable> to match UWP semantics. Left for a human because it is opinionated and could mask real null issues.
